prompts.name: recent-release-crashing-prod
prompts.prompt: Prod has been crashing for the last 10 minutes. We promoted release-20260415 to prod about 15 minutes ago. On-call says roll it back. Walk me through the ConfigHub side.
prompts.expected_output: Pins the suspect immutable ReleaseID/ManifestDigest, controller source, runtime failure, and affected origin annotations. Because the user asked to be walked through the ConfigHub side, it stays coached and makes zero mutation calls: it explains the head-moving rollback using exact prior RevisionID/DataHash values, uses a validated incident slug plus short safe change summary while retaining fuller context in the transcript, and presents each literal command as a separate terminal step. A fresh whole-Space publish is a separate preview and user-run step. It never deploys an old Release directly or bypasses an ApplyGate or explicit external-overlay stop.

prompts.name: traffic-spike-not-from-change
prompts.prompt: We're seeing 5xx from the payments-api in prod. No releases in the last 48 hours, but traffic doubled in the last 30 minutes and Grafana shows pods at CPU limit. What do I do in ConfigHub?
prompts.expected_output: Does not force a rollback narrative. Confirms Release/controller/runtime evidence, treats capacity mitigation as an explicit durable-vs-temporary decision, and previews the smallest ConfigHub replica/resource change if chosen. Because the prompt asks for guidance, it never scales kubectl or submits a mutation; it states the focused decision or concrete stop plus a proof/rollback plan in plain language.

prompts.name: post-incident-cleanup
prompts.prompt: Incident resolved. During the hot window SRE ran `kubectl scale deploy/payments-api -n payments-prod --replicas=12` and edited two configmaps directly. Now ConfigHub shows drift. How do I close out?
prompts.expected_output: Inventories runtime changes read-only, decides which are durable versus temporary, and previews ConfigHub-native mutations with a validated incident slug and short safe summary while retaining fuller context in the transcript. Explains that OCI LiveData is not cluster proof and Argo/Flux may revert out-of-band edits. Previews a resolution Tag with resolution type and closes only after a historical-manifest/controller/runtime receipt.

prompts.name: concurrent-incidents-shared-unit
prompts.prompt: INC-512 and INC-513 both need changes to payments-api right now. Open both incident ChangeSets and get them moving in parallel.
prompts.expected_output: Refuses to interleave two open ChangeSets on the same Unit. Reads current ChangeSet ownership, makes the concurrency conflict explicit, asks the incident commanders to sequence or split non-overlapping scope, and preserves each validated incident slug and safe summary independently while fuller context remains in the transcript. Executes nothing.
